name: live_nullif_with_equal_operands_is_null
description: NULLIF returns NULL when its two operands are equal, so its result is nullable even when the input column is NOT NULL -- proven against a live engine rather than asserted
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
query_sql:
-- @name GetUserNamesExceptAda
-- @returns :many
SELECT u.id, NULLIF(u.name, 'Ada Lovelace') AS maybe_name FROM users u ORDER BY u.id

columns.name: maybe_name
columns.note: NOT NULL in the schema, but NULLIF yields NULL for the row whose name matches the literal

sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc propagates the NOT NULL of the first argument, so NULLIF(name, ...) is typed non-nullable
sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe treats NULLIF as nullable by construction, and this fixture makes an engine return the NULL for the matching row

default: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.com')
INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (2, 'Grace Hopper', 'grace@example.com')
